args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
PREPARED IN ANTICIPATION OF LITIGATION

TO: Deal Team — Capital Markets Practice
FROM: Law Firm Company
RE: Redline Analysis Memorandum — Counterparty Markup of Underwriting Agreement
DATE: [Current Date]
MATTER: Capital Markets — Underwriting Agreement Negotiation

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This memorandum analyzes the counterparty's revision (the "Markup") to our client's draft Underwriting Agreement (the "Original Draft"). We have reconciled the Markup against the Base Materials, the applicable disclosure Schedules and Exhibits, and the firm's capital-markets playbook. We have also applied the controlling deal-team instruction, which supersedes any prior communication.

The counterparty's Markup accepts most firm-standard provisions, but introduces three principal deviations that must be negotiated:

  1. Indemnification — silent reduction of the indemnification cap and conversion of the indemnity basket from a deductible to a tipping basket;
  2. Material Adverse Effect (MAE) — addition of carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter; and
  3. Survival / Limitation Period — shortening of survival for the core representations, contradicting Exhibit B.

Controlling Instruction: Per the latest (controlling) deal-team instruction, the client will CONCEDE the basket conversion from deductible to tipping basket, but treats ANY survival-period reduction as a WALK-AWAY issue. The MAE carve-outs and the indemnification cap are subject to full negotiation, reconciled against the Schedules.

II. BASE MATERIALS AND CONTROLLING DOCUMENTS

The following documents constitute the operative record and are controlling for this analysis:

  • Base Materials (Deal Materials File — Capital Markets): the Original Draft containing representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions.
  • Counterparty Markup (Counterparty Markup — Capital Markets): the counterparty's redline under analysis.
  • Schedules and Exhibits (Schedules and Exhibits — Capital Markets): disclosure schedules qualifying the base materials. Per the governing principle, scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials.
  • Deal Correspondence (Deal Team Correspondence — Capital Markets): partner email thread; only the LATEST message controls the analysis priorities.

III. DEVIATION ANALYSIS

Each deviation introduced by the counterparty's Markup is analyzed below against the Base Materials, the Schedules/Exhibits, and the firm playbook. The party position (Accept / Reject / Counter) for each is set consistent with the controlling instruction.

DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP AND INDEMNITY BASKET

The Markup contains two indemnification changes:

  (a) Indemnification Cap — the counterparty has SILENTLY REDUCED the indemnification cap set in the Base Materials. The firm-standard cap provides a maximum aggregate liability on indemnity claims. The Markup narrows this ceiling.

  (b) Basket Conversion — the Markup converts the indemnity basket from a DEDUCTIBLE (under which the indemnifying party bears the full amount of any liability once the threshold is crossed) to a TIPPING basket (under which only losses in excess of the threshold are recoverable).

Impact and Reconciliation:

  • Schedule 5.2 of the Schedules and Exhibits lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would SILENTLY SHIFT to our client. The reduced cap, in combination with a tipping basket, materially narrows the client's potential recovery on exactly those retained liabilities identified in Schedule 5.2. Because scheduled exceptions control over general statements, the Schedule 5.2 liabilities are decisive in this analysis.

  • Firm Playbook / Negotiation Position: The firm's standard capital-markets position resists both unbargained reductions in the cap and a tipping-basket conversion unless a concession is expressly granted.

  • Controlling Instruction: The client has CONCEDED the basket conversion (deductible → tipping). Accordingly, we will ACCEPT the tipping-basket conversion.

  • Remaining Negotiation: The silent reduction of the indemnification cap is NOT conceded and must be negotiated. We should COUNTER, restoring the cap to the level set in the Base Materials, and expressly memorialize that no retained liabilities on Schedule 5.2 are shifted as a consequence of the basket conversion. The Schedule 5.2 liabilities must remain fully indemnifiable to the original cap.

  Position: Basket conversion — ACCEPT (as conceded); Indemnification cap reduction — REJECT / COUNTER (restore to original level; preserve Schedule 5.2 cover).

DEVIATION 2 — MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT (MAE) DEFINITION — REGULATORY ACTION CARVE-OUTS

The Markup amends the definition of "Material Adverse Effect" to add new carve-outs for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter."

Impact and Reconciliation:

  • Schedule 3.7 of the Schedules and Exhibits discloses TWO PENDING REGULATORY INQUIRIES that intersect directly with the markup's proposed MAE carve-outs. The scheduled exceptions narrow the MAE representation as set out on Schedule 3.7.

  • The markup's additional carve-outs go BEYOND the Schedule 3.7 limitations. By exempting regulatory action of the kind at issue, the counterparty effectively removes MAE protection for the very regulatory developments that Schedule 3.7 flags as active risks. This materially hollows out the MAE representation for our client and would leave the two pending inquiries outside Client's protection.

  • Because scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials, the scope of the MAE carve-outs must be judged against Schedule 3.7. The markup's carve-outs are overbroad relative to the scheduled exceptions.

  Negotiation Position: REJECT the markup's added MAE carve-outs as drafted. COUNTER with an MAE definition whose carve-outs are strictly limited to, and no broader than, the specific matters disclosed on Schedule 3.7, and that expressly preserve the client's protection for any regulatory action that has a material adverse effect beyond the scope of those two disclosed inquiries.

  Position: REJECT / COUNTER — limit MAE carve-outs to the precise Schedule 3.7 disclosures; do not allow a general regulatory-action exemption.

DEVIATION 3 — SURVIVAL / LIMITATION PERIOD FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS

The Markup introduces a NEW limitation period that SHORTENS SURVIVAL for the core representations (representations and warranties).

Impact and Reconciliation:

  • Exhibit B of the Schedules and Exhibits sets the SURVIVAL MATRIX for the transaction. The markup's limitation-period change directly CONTRADICTS Exhibit B. The scheduled exhibit is controlling: any survival period that departs from Exhibit B is contrary to the agreed schedule.

  • Shortening survival of the core representations would deprive the client of its remedy window under the express agreement. Core representations customarily survive for a defined, agreed period; the base materials and Exhibit B reflect that agreed period.

  Controlling Instruction: The client treats ANY survival-period reduction as a WALK-AWAY issue. This is the firm's red-line, non-negotiable position.

  Negotiation Position: REJECT any survival-period reduction outright. The survival matrix in Exhibit B is controlling and must be preserved in full. This is a WALK-AWAY issue per the controlling instruction — no concession is available and no counter will be offered. If the counterparty maintains the reduction, the transaction cannot proceed.

  Position: REJECT (WALK-AWAY) — Exhibit B survival matrix controls; no reduction acceptable.

IV. RECONCILIATION SUMMARY TABLE

  Deviation                 | Position        | Rationale / Controlling Authority
  --------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------------
  1. Indemnification cap    | REJECT/COUNTER | Silent reduction; Schedule 5.2 liabilities would be shifted; not conceded
  1. Basket conversion      | ACCEPT         | Conceded per controlling deal-team instruction
  2. MAE regulatory         | REJECT/COUNTER | Carve-outs overbroad vs. Schedule 3.7; leaves disclosed inquiries unprotected
     carve-outs
  3. Survival reduction     | REJECT         | Contradicts Exhibit B; WALK-AWAY per controlling instruction; no concession

V. NEGOTIATION-READY RECOMMENDATIONS

  1. ACCEPT the conversion of the indemnity basket from a deductible to a tipping basket (conceded by client).
  2. COUNTER the silent reduction of the indemnification cap; restore the cap to the level in the Base Materials and confirm in writing that the retained liabilities on Schedule 5.2 remain covered to the original cap without shift.
  3. REJECT the markup's MAE carve-outs for regulatory action; COUNTER with carve-outs limited strictly to the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.7, preserving client protection for any regulatory action beyond those disclosures.
  4. REJECT any survival-period reduction; preserve the Exhibit B survival matrix in full. This is a walk-away issue — no concession and no counter.

VI. OPEN ITEMS / NEXT STEPS

  • Circulate the memo to the capital-markets partner and confirm alignment on the walk-away position regarding survival before the next counterparty call.
  • Obtain client sign-off on the basket-conversion concession (already indicated as conceded in the controlling instruction).
  • Prepare conforming mark-up language for the MAE definition and survival provision reflecting the positions above.
  • Flag Schedule 5.2 and Schedule 3.7 disclosures in the negotiation brief so that no scheduled exception is inadvertently overridden.

                              * * *

This memorandum is privileged and confidential and prepared in anticipation of negotiation; it reflects the analysis of the counterparty markup against the base materials, the governing schedules and exhibits, and the controlling deal-team instruction taken as of the date of the latest communication.
